title: Impact of veriflex and ICL on corneal biomechanics and endothelial cell density

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License)

indication: Moderate to high myopia, age 21-45 years, stable refraction; eyes with abnormal cornea, endothelial dystrophy, preoperative ECD below 2600 cells/mm2, anterior segment pathology, uveitis, glaucoma or ACD below 3.00 mm excluded

groups.description: Group I: 58 eyes of 30 patients implanted with the Veriflex foldable iris-fixated (iris-claw) anterior chamber phakic IOL by enclavation; standard procedure and postoperative care
Group II: 59 eyes of 30 patients implanted with the EVO ICL V4c (central KS-Aquaport) posterior chamber phakic IOL; standard procedure and postoperative care

series.baseline_label: Preoperative ECD of the operated eye (Table 2 row 'Preoperative'; Methods: Topcon EM-3000 specular microscopy preoperatively)
series.notes: Table 2 column 'Group I (Veriflex)'; mean ± SD (the Abstract and Results describe these values as mean ECD). Per-visit n not tabulated.

series.baseline_label: Preoperative ECD of the operated eye (Table 2 row 'Preoperative'; Methods: Topcon EM-3000 specular microscopy preoperatively)
series.notes: Table 2 column 'Group II (ICL)'; mean ± SD (the Abstract and Results describe these values as mean ECD). Per-visit n not tabulated.

exclusions.what: Table 2 rows 'Change from Baseline (cells/mm2) ± SD' and 'Percentage Change'
exclusions.reason: The same table gives absolute ECD for both groups; the absolute ECD series are used

exclusions.what: Table 2 'P-value (Between Groups)' column and 'P-value (Within Group)' row

exclusions.reason: Same preoperative values as Table 2; Table 2 cells are cited for the whole series

notes: Two established phakic IOL designs compared without an investigational agent: both groups are control-role, separate groups (protocol: two standard techniques compared).
Both eyes of most patients were included (117 eyes of 60 patients); n counts eyes.
Surgeries in the two groups were performed by different surgeons (Methods).
